[Judgment of the Court was made by MRS.V.BHAVANI SUBBAROYAN.J.] CMP(MD)No.1656 of 2024 in CMA(MD)SR.No.53965 of 2023 is filed to condone the delay of 201 days in filing the appeal against the judgment and decree dated 12.08.2022 made in Ar.O.P.No.113 of 2016.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and 2.

The 1st respondent herein is the claimant whose lands measuring an extent of 61.774 cents [2500 square meters] comprised in Survey Nos.20/3B-1350 and 20/3D-1150 sq.mts situate at Dindigul District, Nilakottai Taluk, Kanavaipatti Village, were acquired by the 2nd respondent herein/competent authority for land acquisition, for formation of National Highways.
The appellant is the beneficiary of the National Highways.
The competent authority fixed Rs.1500/- per cent along with 10% appreciation value and awarded a total compensation of Rs. 1,01,959/- for 61.774 cents of the 1st respondent.

The 1st respondent received the said compensation amount under protest and thereafter filed an appeal before the 3rd respondent herein, contending that even before the acquisition proceedings, the adjacent lands of the 1st respondent were converted as house sites and sold for higher value.
However, the 3rd respondent dismissed the appeal confirming the award passed by the 2nd respondent/competent authority.
Aggrieved by the same, the 1st respondents/claimant filed Arbitration Original Petition No.113/2016 before the learned Principal District Judge, Dindigul.
In the said Ar.O.P., the 1st respondent examined herself as PW1 and marked four documents.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and 3.

Before the Court below, the 1st respondent/claimant contended that the 2nd respondent/competent authority has considered only 47 sales out of 1077 sales during the period of The Project Director vs R.Murugeswari on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172711725/
2 one year between 29.03.2011 and 28.03.2012 and fixed the marked value at Rs.41.35 sq.ft and awarded compensation of Rs.1,01,959/-.
The 1st respondent also marked Ex.P3 to prove her contention that her adjacent lands were sold for sufficiently higher value than the value fixed by the compentent authority.

The learned Judge, finding that Ex.P3 sale deed dated 28.09.2011 was registered just five months prior to the date of publication of 3-A1 notification and that the respondents 2 and 3 have not chosen to disprove the contents of Ex.P3 nor produced any supporting documents to substantiate their fixation of market value, by order dated 12.08.2022 in Ar.O.P.No.113 of 2016, has fixed the value of the acquired land as per Ex.P3 at Rs.1,614/- per square metre and after deducting 1/3 rd towards developmental charges, has enhanced compensation to Rs.29,59,000/- as against Rs.1,01,959/- awarded by the 2nd respondent and confirmed by the 3rd respondent.
As against the said order, the appellant has filed this appeal with the delay of 201 days.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and

4. As regards the delay of 201 days in filing this appeal, learned counsel for the appellant submitted that order copy was made ready on 11.10.2022 but due to inadvertence, the above delay occurred and therefore prayed to condone the delay.

5. On the merits of the case, it is the main bone of contention of the learned counsel for the appellant that it is a well settled law that reappraisal of evidence by the Court under Section 34 of the Arbitration & Conciliation Act, 1996, is not permissible and therefore, the Court below ought not to have examined as to whether the reasons recorded by the compentent authority are right or erroneous.

He further submitted that as per Section 34(2) of the Act, the learned Judge has limited powers and can set aside the arbitral award only on the grounds namely, incapacity of party,
invalidity of agreement, notice not given to party, unable to present case and award beyond scope of reference.

However, in the present case, the Court below bent upon to examine the reasons recorded by the competent authority ignoring its limited powers conferred https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and under Section 32(2) and therefore, the impugned order is liable to be set aside.

Learned counsel also contended that it would not be open for the Court below in the proceedings under Section 34 of the Act, to modify the award and the appropriate course to be adoped is to set aside the award and remit the matter to the Arbitrator in terms of Section 34(4) for fresh adjudication.

In support of the said proposition, learned counsel relied on the following decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court:-
(i) National Highways Authority of India vs. Sri P.Nagaraju @ Cheluvaiah and another [C.A.No.4671 of 2022, dated 11.07.2022]
(ii) Project Director, National Highways Authority of India vs. M.Hakeem and another reported in 2021 SCC Online SC 473.
6.

3 stating that inadvertently delay occurred, absolutely no reason has been assigned by the appellant.
Time and again, Courts have held that each and every day delay should be explained with sufficient cause, but in this case that is conspicuously absent.

Even on merits learned counsel contended that though acquisition proceedings were initiated in the year 2012, award was passed in 2014, award was enhanced in 2022, till date, the 1st respondent is not paid with the enhanced compensation.
7. We have heard the learned counsels for the appellant as well as the respondents.

8. Before considering the delay condonation petition, we deem fit to extract the expression of ''sufficient cause'' by the Apex Court in Borse Brothers Engineers and Contractors Private Limited's case [cited supra].

Paragraph 58 of the said judgment is extracted below for better https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and appreciation of the case on hand:-
''58.

Given the object sought to be achieved under both the Arbitration Act and the Commercial Courts Act, that is, the speedy resolution of disputes, the expression sufficient cause is not elastic enough to cover long delays beyond the period provided by the appeal provision itself.
Besides, the expression sufficient cause is not itself a loose panacea for the ill of pressing negligent and stale claims.

This Court,
in Basawaraj v. Land Acquisition Officer, (2013) 14 SCC 81, has held:
9. Sufficient cause is the cause for which the defendant could not be blamed for his absence.

entities.text: Basawaraj v. Land Acquisition Officer, (2013) 14 SCC 81
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The meaning of the word sufficient is adequate or enough, inasmuch as may be necessary to answer the purpose intended.

Therefore, the word sufficient embraces no more than that which provides a platitude, which when the act done suffices to accomplish the purpose intended in the facts and circumstances existing in a case, duly examined from the viewpoint of a reasonable standard of a cautious man.

In this context, sufficient cause means that the party should not have acted in a negligent manner or there was a want of bona fide on its part in view of the facts and circumstances of a case or it cannot be alleged that the party has not acted diligently or remained inactive.

However, the facts and circumstances of each case must afford sufficient ground to enable the court concerned to exercise discretion for the reason that whenever the court exercises discretion, it has to be exercised judiciously.

The applicant must satisfy the court that he was prevented by any sufficient cause from prosecuting his case, and unless a satisfactory explanation is furnished, the court should not allow the application for condonation of delay.

and merely a device to cover an ulterior purpose.

(See Manindra Land and Building Corpn. Ltd. v. Bhutnath Banerjee [AIR 1964 SC 1336] , Mata Din v. A. Narayanan [(1969) 2 SCC 770 : AIR 1970 SC 1953] , Parimal v.

9. While dealing with the appeals filed under Section 37 of the Arbitration & Conciliation Act, 1996 with the delay, the Apex in the very same judgment has held as follows:-
''63.

Given the aforesaid and the object of speedy disposal sought to be achieved both under the Arbitration Act and the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and Commercial Courts Act, for appeals filed under section 37 of the Arbitration Act that are governed by Articles 116 and 117 of the Limitation Act or section 13(1A) of the Commercial Courts Act, a delay beyond 90 days, 30 days or 60 days, respectively, is to be condoned by way of exception and not by way of rule.

In a fit case in which a party has otherwise acted bona fide and not in a negligent manner, a short delay beyond such period can, in the discretion of the court, be condoned, always bearing in mind that the other side of the picture is that the opposite party may have acquired both in equity and justice, what may now be lost by the first partys inaction, negligence or laches.''

10. In Borse Brothers Engineers and Contractors Private Limited's case [cited supra], though there was 75 days delay beyond the period of 60 days provided by the Commercial Courts Act, the Apex Court declined to condone the delay, and held as follows:-
''65.

entities.text: Borse Brothers Engineers and Contractors Private Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Apart from this, there is a long delay of 131 days beyond the 60- day period provided for filing an appeal under section 13(1A) of the Commercial Courts Act.
There is no explanation worth the name contained in the condonation of delay application, beyond the usual file-pushing and administrative exigency.
This appeal is therefore dismissed.
67. That apart, on the facts of this appeal, there is a long delay of 75 days beyond the period of 60 days provided by the Commercial Courts Act.

Despite the fact that a certified copy of the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and District Courts judgment was obtained by the respondent on 27.04.2019, the appeal was filed only on The Project Director vs R.Murugeswari on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172711725/
5 09.09.2019, the explanation for delay being:
2.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That, the certified copy of the order dated 01/04/2013 was received by the appellant on 27/04/2019.
Thereafter the matter was placed before the CGM purchase MPPKVVCL for the compliance of the order.
The same was then sent to the law officer, MPPKVVCL for opinion.
3. That after taking opinion for appeal, and approval of the concerned authorities, the officer-in-charge was appointed vide order dated 23/07/2019.

4. That, thereafter due to bulky records of the case and for procurement of the necessary documents some delay has been caused however, the appeal has been prepared and filed to pursuant to the same and further delay.

5. That due to the aforesaid procedural approval and since the appellant is a public entity formed under the Energy department of the State Government, the delay caused in filing the appeal is bonafide and which deserve[s] to be condoned.
68. This explanation falls woefully short of making out any sufficient cause.
This appeal is therefore allowed and the condonation of delay is set aside on this score also.
69. In the Civil Appeal arising out of SLP (C) Diary No. 18079 of 2020, there is a huge delay of 227 days in filing the appeal, and a 200-day delay in refiling.
The facts of this case also show that there was no sufficient cause whatsoever to condone such a long delay.

The impugned judgment of the High Court of Delhi dated 15.10.2019 cannot be faulted on this score and this appeal is consequently dismissed.''
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and 11.

Reverting to the case on hand, with regard to condonation of 201 days delay in filing this appeal,
the appellant has assigned the following reason at paragrpah 14 which reads as follows:-
''14.

I humbly submit that the Learned District Judge, Dindigul made the order on 12.08.2022 and copy was made ready on 11.10.2022 and the present Appeal under section 37 of the act ought to have been filed within 90 days from thereon.
Inadvertently, there is delay in filing the present CMA.

Therefore, the delay may be condoned for the above stated reasons.''
12.
Perusal of the said extracted portion reveals that absolutely no reason has been assigned by the appellant muchless the sufficient reason.
The appellant has not even chosen to offer the usual file pushing and administrative exigency as reasons for the delay, whereas, they have simply stated that inadvertantly delay occurred.

Though in Borse Brothers Engineers and Contractors Private Limited's case, the Apex Court held that in a fit case, in which, a party has otherwise acted bona fide and not in a The Project Director vs R.Murugeswari on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172711725/
6 negligent manner, a short delay beyond such period can, in the discretion of the court, be condoned by way of exception, always bearing in mind the other side of the picture, in the case on hand, the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and reason is assigned in a casual manner that inadvertantly, there is a delay of 201 days in filing the appeal.

Hence, this Court is not inclined to condone the delay.
13. Accordingly, the delay condonation petition in CMP(MD)No.1656 of 2024 is dismissed.
Consequently, CMA(MD)SR.No.53965 of 2023 is rejected.
